h1:
Samut Prakan With Kids
Crocodile Farm + Ancient City in 2 Days
intro: Samut Prakan is one of the easiest places to take kids near Bangkok — under an hour by car, but with a crocodile farm and its catch shows, an Ancient City so big children can run all day, a giant three-headed elephant, and seagulls that eat right out of your hand. We've laid this out as a relaxed 2-day plan, with naptime and car snoozes built in.

blocks.html: If you've got little kids at home over a long weekend and don't want a long drive, Samut Prakan is the answer a lot of families overlook. The headline spots — the crocodile farm, the Ancient City, and the Erawan Museum — sit no more than 15–20 minutes apart, so you can loop them all in a single day. But with young kids we'd spread it over 2 days; it's far less tiring. This plan is built so children get to see animals, run around, eat, and take breaks along the way.

blocks.title: Overall entry fees (check before you go)
blocks.html: Ticket prices change often, so check the official pages before you leave the house. Rough current figures: Crocodile Farm adults around 100–150 THB, kids cheaper · Ancient City Thai adults 400, kids (6–14) 200 THB · Erawan Museum Thai adults around 300, kids around 150 THB · Bang Pu free entry, you only pay for the pork rinds to feed the birds.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Crocodiles, the three-headed elephant, and seagulls

blocks.html: Start day one with the stuff kids get excited about. Hit the crocodile farm early to catch a show time, follow with the Erawan Museum around midday, then close out with sunset and bird-feeding at Bang Pu. It's a day full of animals and room to run.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Big animals + the sea at dusk

items.activity: Arrive at the Samut Prakan Crocodile Farm and Zoo (open 08:00–18:00 daily)
items.note: Check the croc-wrestling show schedule at the entrance, then wander the other animals while you wait — there are hippos, monkeys, and peacocks too.
Kids love it, but it's pretty loud and crowded. If your child startles easily, sit toward the back and hold their hand.

items.activity: Lunch inside the farm or at a restaurant around Samrong
items.note: The farm has snacks but they're pricey. You can head out to an à la carte spot instead — there are plenty nearby.

items.activity: Erawan Museum — a copper three-headed elephant as tall as a 14-story building
items.note: It's cool and comfortable inside, and you can walk up into the elephant's belly. Carry little ones on the stairs and no running — the floors are slippery and there are antiques around.

items.activity: Drive to Bang Pu Recreation Center (free entry, open 05:30–20:00)
items.note: Buy a bag of pork rinds for 10 THB, walk out over the sea on the Suk Ta pier, and toss them to the gulls. Birds are thickest from Nov–Apr.

items.activity: Watch the sunset from Suk Ta pier + dinner at the seaside Suk Jai Pavilion
items.note: It gets windy, so pack a windbreaker for the kids. Some stretches of walkway are narrow — keep hold of little hands the whole time.

blocks.title: About the seagulls
blocks.html: The gulls really do migrate in large numbers from late October through April. Come outside that window and you'll see fewer of them, but Bang Pu is still a fine seaside stroll and dinner spot — you won't feel cheated.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Samut Prakan trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: Day 2 — The Ancient City, all day

blocks.html: The Ancient City is so vast kids can run around it all day. It's an open-air museum that recreates temples, palaces, and traditional Thai houses from across the country in one place. For families, the big draw is that there's a tram and a sightseeing bus to ride, plus bikes and golf carts to rent — no walking until the kids melt down. Plan for the whole day and go early to dodge the afternoon heat.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Tour all of Thailand in one day

items.activity: Arrive at the Ancient City (open 09:00–19:00 daily · Thai adults 400, kids 200)
items.note: Grab a map at the entrance. There's a free sightseeing bus and rental points for bikes/golf carts. With young kids, a golf cart is easier to manage.

items.activity: Take a first loop around by ride to get the lay of the land
items.note: See which zones the kids gravitate to, then come back and explore those on foot — that way you're not wandering aimlessly until everyone's worn out.

items.activity: Walk the old floating market zone + central-Thailand houses
items.note: There's old-style food and Thai sweets for the kids to try, and a few spots have ducks and fish in the canal to watch.

items.activity: Lunch break inside the Ancient City
items.note: There are restaurants in several zones. Midday sun is harsh — find a long shady spot and let the kids nap for a bit.

items.activity: Rent Thai costumes for a family photo (if you're keen)
items.note: There are traditional Thai outfits to rent — kids look adorable in them, and they photograph beautifully against the old houses and replica temples.

items.activity: Cycle / golf-cart through the northern and northeastern zones
items.note: Lots of shade here and a cooler breeze than the morning. Older kids can pedal themselves; little ones ride along.

items.activity: Stop at Phra Samut Chedi on the way back (it's close by)
items.note: A white stupa at the river mouth — a quick prayer, riverside photos, and an easy way to wrap up the trip.

blocks.text: Add-on spots if you have a Day 3 or it's a long weekend

blocks.html: If you're going on a Saturday or Sunday and want to tack on an easy half-day, cross over to the Bang Krachao side. The air is cleaner and the pace slower than in town — a nice way to close out the trip before heading home.

items.name: Bang Nam Phueng Floating Market
items.blurb: Open Saturdays and Sundays only, with loads of food. Rent a bike to ride around the community for 30 THB/hour, or 100 THB/day.

items.name: Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park
items.blurb: A large public park in Bang Krachao where you can cycle past forest and ponds. Open daily, shady, and great for letting kids run around.

items.name: Wat Bang Phli Yai Nai
items.blurb: Home to a big reclining-style Buddha, with the old Bang Phli market right next door — wander and eat well along the canal.

blocks.text: Tips for taking kids around Samut Prakan

items: Start early — both the crocodile farm and the Ancient City are largely outdoors. Mornings are cooler, so kids stay happy longer.
Pack sun gear and water — hats, sunscreen, drinking water, cooling towels, especially on the Ancient City day with all that outdoor walking.
Build in naptime — both days have longer drives, so kids can snooze in the car and arrive at the next stop in a better mood.
Bring a stroller or carrier — the Ancient City and the Erawan Museum involve a lot of walking; little ones definitely won't manage on foot.
Carry cash — pork rinds at Bang Pu, market food, and some parking spots are easier with cash.

blocks.title: Getting there without a car
blocks.html: You can take the BTS Sukhumvit line to the end of the line — say Kheha station — then grab a taxi or motorbike taxi to each spot. But the sights are spread out and outdoors, so with young kids, having your own car or a rental makes things a lot smoother.

faq.q: How many days should you spend in Samut Prakan with kids?
faq.a: One day is enough to hit the highlights, since the crocodile farm, the Ancient City, and the Erawan Museum are close together. But with young kids, 2 days is more comfortable — it leaves room for naps and keeps you from rushing.

faq.q: Is the Samut Prakan Crocodile Farm open daily, and when are the shows?
faq.a: It's open every day, 08:00–18:00. There are crocodile-catching shows and animal performances at intervals throughout the day. Check the schedule at the entrance so you can time your visit to catch a show.

faq.q: Is there a lot of walking at the Ancient City? Can young kids handle it?
faq.a: It's a huge area, and on foot alone young kids won't manage. But there's a free sightseeing bus, and you can rent bikes and golf carts. For families with little ones, a golf cart is the easiest to manage and the least tiring.

faq.q: Can you feed the seagulls at Bang Pu all year round?
faq.a: The gulls migrate in large numbers from late October through April; outside that season you'll see fewer of them. Bang Pu is free to enter — you only pay 10 THB per bag of pork rinds. Even off-season, it's still a nice spot for a seaside stroll and dinner.

faq.q: Can you visit Samut Prakan without your own car?
faq.a: Yes — take the BTS Sukhumvit line to the end of the line, then a taxi or motorbike taxi. But the sights are spread out and outdoors, so with young kids, having a car or a rental is a lot more convenient.
